name: UC3845D8TR
title: UCx84x current-mode PWM controllers (UC1842 to UC3845); UC3845D8TR: UC3845 in SOIC-8 on tape and reel
summary: A family of fixed-frequency peak current-mode PWM controllers for off-line and DC-DC converters that drive an external N-channel MOSFET from a 1 A totem-pole output. Each has a trimmed 5 V reference, an error amplifier with a 2.5 V internal reference, a current-sense comparator with a 1 V maximum threshold for cycle-by-cycle current limiting, an RC-set oscillator to 500 kHz and undervoltage lockout drawing under 1 mA before start. The twelve parts differ in temperature grade, UVLO thresholds (16/10 V or 8.4/7.6 V) and maximum duty cycle (about 100 % or 50 %). The UC3845D8TR is the UC3845 (0 to 70 °C, 8.4 V on / 7.6 V off, 50 % maximum duty, OUTPUT at half the oscillator frequency) in an 8-pin SOIC on a 2500-piece reel.
key_figures: ±1 A peak; rise and fall 25 ns typ into 1 nF
up to 500 kHz; 52 kHz typ at 10 kΩ, 3.3 nF
12 to 28 V recommended; 30 V absolute maximum

notes: The family name is UCabcd: the first digit after UC is the temperature grade (1: -55 to 125 °C, 2: -40 to 85 °C, 3: 0 to 70 °C); the last digit is the variant (2 and 4: UVLO 16 V on / 10 V off; 3 and 5: 8.4 V on / 7.6 V off; 2 and 3: duty cycle to 100 %; 4 and 5: duty cycle to 50 %).

Package codes in the orderable numbers: D8 is the 8-pin SOIC, D the 14-pin SOIC, N the 8-pin PDIP (P), J the 8-pin CDIP (JG), W the 14-pin CFP and L the 20-pin LCCC (FK); TR parts come on 2500-piece reels.
UC3845D8TR: UC3845 in the 8-pin SOIC, 2500 per large reel, Active, 0 to 70 °C, marked UC3845.
Other qualified versions of the family exist as catalog, enhanced-product (UC1845A-EP), military and space (-SP) parts.

pins.name: COMP
pins.function: Error amplifier output, for the compensation network. The amplifier output is current limited, so pulling COMP to GROUND from outside forces zero duty cycle.

pins.name: VFB
pins.function: Inverting input of the error amplifier; the non-inverting input is held internally at 2.5 V. Keep the trace short and its stray capacitance low.

pins.name: ISENSE
pins.function: Current sense input to the PWM comparator, taken from the resistor in the MOSFET source; when it reaches the level set by COMP, the on-time ends. A ramp applied to this pin instead gives voltage-mode control or slope compensation.

pins.name: RT/CT
pins.function: Oscillator timing node: RRT from VREF and CCT to GROUND set the frequency (fOSC ≈ 1.72 / (RRT × CCT)). RRT must not be below 5 kΩ. Route the CCT return straight and short to GROUND, apart from other ground currents where possible.

pins.name: GROUND
pins.function: Analog ground; where there is no PWRGND pin it is the power ground as well.

pins.name: OUTPUT
pins.function: Totem-pole gate drive for an external N-channel MOSFET, up to 1 A peak source and sink. Held low actively while VCC is below the turn-on threshold.

pins.name: VCC
pins.function: Supply input of the controller. Its current is the quiescent current plus the average gate-drive current (Qg × fSW). Needs a ceramic bypass of typically 0.1 µF straight to GROUND, and a second capacitor of at least ten times the MOSFET gate capacitance.

circuits.title: Simplified application (boost converter with UC2843)
circuits.description: A non-isolated step-up converter. The inductor runs from VIN to the drain of the MOSFET, and the diode carries its current on to the output when the switch turns off. A resistor from VIN feeds VCC, which has its own capacitor. The MOSFET source returns through the sense resistor, whose top goes straight to ISENSE. RT and CT on VREF and RT/CT set the oscillator; VREF has its own capacitor. The output divider brings the output back to VFB, and a resistor and capacitor in parallel from VFB to COMP close the loop.

circuits.title: Current-sense circuit (Figure 7-3)
circuits.description: The switch current flows down through RCS to ground. RCSF and CCSF form a low-pass filter between the top of RCS and the ISENSE pin, so the turn-on spike does not end the cycle early.

circuits.title: Error-amplifier configuration (Figure 7-4)
circuits.description: The general form of the voltage loop on the primary side: an input impedance ZI from the sensed voltage into VFB, and a feedback impedance ZF from COMP back to VFB. COMP can deliver or absorb as much as 0.5 mA.

circuits.title: Providing power to the UCx84x (Figure 7-7)
circuits.description: Off-line bias. The rectified line charges CIN; RSTART trickles current (at least 1 mA) from the bulk rail into CVCC until VCC reaches the turn-on threshold. Once switching starts, the auxiliary winding NA supplies VCC through DBIAS. A 0.1 µF ceramic sits beside CVCC at the VCC pin. OUTPUT drives the MOSFET, whose source returns to ground through RCS.

parts.note: dots on the NP bulk end, the NS lower end and the NA ground end

circuits.title: Oscillator section (Figure 7-8)
circuits.description: RRT from VREF charges CCT on RT/CT; CCT returns to GROUND. For RRT above 5 kΩ the frequency is about 1.72 / (RRT × CCT).

circuits.title: Synchronizing the oscillator (Figure 7-9)
circuits.description: CCT returns to ground through a 24 Ω resistor instead of directly. A sync pulse driven across that resistor lifts the CCT voltage past the upper oscillator threshold and starts a new cycle. RRT and CCT are set for a free-running frequency below the sync rate (typically 20 % lower, with a 0.5 V pulse across the resistor).

circuits.title: Shutdown techniques: latched shutdown through ISENSE (Figure 7-10, left)
circuits.description: A pulse on the SCR gate fires it; the SCR pulls the PNP base down through 30 Ω, the PNP turns on from VREF and drives ISENSE above 1 V, ending every cycle. The 1 kΩ holds the PNP off otherwise, and 500 Ω joins ISENSE to the current-sense resistor. The SCR stays on until VCC drops below the UVLO off threshold and VREF collapses.

circuits.title: Shutdown techniques: pulling COMP low (Figure 7-10, right)
circuits.description: An NPN from COMP to ground, driven at its base by the SHUTDOWN signal. When it conducts, COMP falls below two diode drops and the output stops.

circuits.title: Slope compensation (Figure 7-11)
circuits.description: An NPN follower buffers the oscillator ramp on RT/CT; its emitter feeds RRAMP into the ISENSE node, where it adds to the current signal arriving through RCSF from the top of RCS. CCSF filters ISENSE. VREF has a 0.1 µF capacitor. For the UCx842 and UCx843.

circuits.title: Soft-start circuitry (Figure 7-12)
circuits.description: RSS charges CSS from VREF. A PNP with its base on that node and its emitter on COMP holds COMP down near the capacitor voltage, so the duty cycle widens from zero as CSS charges; once it is charged the PNP is off and out of the loop.

circuits.title: Current-mode PWM used as a voltage-mode PWM (Figure 7-13)
circuits.description: A 2N2907 current source (base set by a 1N4148 and two resistors from VREF, emitter resistor to VREF) charges CCT on RT/CT to make the sawtooth. A 2N2222 follower takes the ramp from RT/CT and feeds it through 2.7 kΩ into a 1 kΩ to ground at ISENSE, so the PWM compares the error voltage with this sawtooth instead of the switch current.

circuits.title: Open-loop laboratory test fixture (Figure 8-1)
circuits.description: A bench fixture for running the controller without a power stage. A 1 kΩ potentiometer between two 4.7 kΩ resistors across VREF sets VFB (E/A adjust), with 100 kΩ from VFB to COMP. R1 and CRTCT set the oscillator. An NPN follower samples the RT/CT ramp into a 5 kΩ potentiometer whose wiper drives ISENSE (ISENSE adjust). VREF and VCC each have 0.1 µF to ground, and OUTPUT has a 1 kΩ load that a switch returns to VCC or to ground.

parts.note: returns the load to VCC or ground; pins COM, A, B

circuits.title: Typical application: 48 W off-line flyback, 85 to 265 VAC in, 12 V at 4 A out (Figure 8-2)
circuits.description: A continuous-conduction flyback built on the UC2842 at 110 kHz. A fuse in one line lead feeds the bridge; the bridge and 180 µF bulk capacitor feed the primary of a 1.5 mH transformer (NP:NS = 10, NP:NA = 10) switched by QSW, with an RCD clamp (10 nF, 50 kΩ, DCLAMP) across the primary. RSTART (100 kΩ) charges the 120 µF VCC capacitor; the auxiliary winding then supplies VCC through 22 Ω and DBIAS. OUTPUT drives the gate through 10 Ω with a 10 kΩ bleeder, and two Schottky diodes clamp OUTPUT to VCC and ground. The 0.75 Ω RCS sets a 1.36 A peak; RCSF (4.2 kΩ) and CCSF (100 pF) filter ISENSE, and an NPN follower on RT/CT injects the oscillator ramp through 10 nF and 24.9 kΩ for slope compensation. On the secondary a Schottky and 2200 µF give 12 V; a TL431 with a 9.53 kΩ / 2.49 kΩ divider and an 88.7 kΩ + 0.01 µF zero drives the optocoupler LED through 1.3 kΩ. The opto transistor runs from VREF into VFB through 4.99 kΩ, with 1 kΩ to ground, and the error amplifier's 10 kΩ ∥ 10 nF from COMP to VFB adds the pole. RSS, CSS and a PNP on COMP give soft start.

operation.text: The twelve devices differ in three ways: temperature grade (UC184x -55 to 125 °C, UC284x -40 to 85 °C, UC384x 0 to 70 °C); UVLO thresholds (UCx842 and UCx844 turn on at 16 V and off at 10 V, for off-line supplies; UCx843 and UCx845 at 8.4 V and 7.6 V, for regulated DC inputs); and maximum duty cycle (UCx842 and UCx843 up to about 100 %; UCx844 and UCx845 up to 50 %). The UC3845 is the 0 to 70 °C, 8.4 V / 7.6 V, 50 % member.

Fixed-frequency peak current-mode PWM. The oscillator sets the PWM latch and turns OUTPUT on; the switch current, seen as a voltage on ISENSE, rises until it meets the error amplifier output divided down through an internal 2R/R network, and the latch resets. The highest ISENSE level that can end a cycle is 1 V typical. Clamping the error voltage therefore caps the peak current on every cycle, which is the pulse-by-pulse current limit. The latch is reset-dominant, so a pulse cannot restart until the next clock (no double pulsing).
An internal T flip-flop blanks OUTPUT on every other oscillator cycle, so OUTPUT switches at half the oscillator frequency and the duty cycle cannot exceed 50 %.

Until VCC passes VCCON the output stage is off and the IC draws under 1 mA (0.5 mA typical); above it the supply current rises to 11 mA typical, 17 mA maximum, plus gate drive. Below VCCOFF switching stops and VREF returns to 0 V. During lockout the driver is high impedance and sinks only a little current; a resistor from gate to source of the MOSFET keeps leakage from turning it on. The 6 V hysteresis of the UCx842/UCx844 keeps an off-line bootstrap supply from oscillating at start-up; the narrower window of the UCx843/UCx845 suits regulated inputs.

A resistor RSTART from the rectified line charges CVCC to the turn-on threshold; after start the auxiliary winding NA supplies VCC through DBIAS. With the 1 mA start-up current, RSTART can be up to 100 kΩ and still start the supply at 90 VRMS; it then dissipates under 350 mW at 130 VRMS. CVCC must hold VCC above the off threshold until the output comes into regulation.

VCC has an internal zener clamp (30 V min, 39 V typ at 25 mA), but the absolute maximum from a low-impedance source is 30 V, so a supply above the recommended 12 to 28 V range is fed through a series resistor (Equation 5). An electrolytic plus a ceramic on VCC, both near the pins, keep noise out.

VREF is the 5 V reference (±2 %), the logic supply of the fast internal circuits, and the source of the RRT charging current; it is short-circuit limited. It needs at least 0.1 µF ceramic at the pin, more for external loads, and may have an electrolytic as well. When VCC is above 1 V but below the turn-on threshold, a 5 kΩ internal resistor holds VREF low, so VREF serves as a power-good / UVLO status signal.

RRT from VREF charges CCT; an internal discharge current (typically 6 mA at room temperature) resets it, and the discharge time is the dead time during which OUTPUT is held low (Figure 6-9). The RT/CT ramp is 1.7 V peak-to-peak with an upper threshold near 2.7 V. Recommended ranges are RRT 5 kΩ to 100 kΩ and CCT 1 nF to 100 nF; RRT below 5 kΩ makes the frequency drift with temperature and tolerances. Dead time should stay under 15 % of the clock period. Operation is possible to 500 kHz.

At high duty cycle the RT/CT voltage is near its threshold when the switch turns off, and the turn-off spike can end the cycle early. Use as large a CCT as the dead time allows, never much below 1000 pF, and clamp OUTPUT with a Schottky diode from GROUND so that the gate drive pulled below ground does not couple into the oscillator.

A bipolar totem pole sinks and sources up to 1 A peak and drives a MOSFET gate directly. Schottky diodes from OUTPUT to the supply and to ground may be needed against overshoot and undershoot. A gate-to-source bleeder resistor keeps the MOSFET off during lockout, and an external clamp protects the gate when VCC is above the gate voltage rating.

The amplifier drives COMP from an open-collector stage paralleled by a current source (about 0.5 mA either way), with 1 MHz unity-gain bandwidth and low output resistance, so the compensation network can sit from COMP to VFB. The non-inverting input is the reference divided to 2.5 V. For secondary-side regulation through an optocoupler, VFB is grounded so that COMP sits high and sources about 0.8 mA, and the opto transistor pulls COMP down directly. For primary-side regulation a divider of the output goes to VFB with the compensation between VFB and COMP.

RCS in the MOSFET source turns the switch current into a voltage on ISENSE, which is the non-inverting input of the PWM comparator; the internal gain from ISENSE to the error signal is 3 V/V, and the trip level is 1 V typical, so the peak current is about 1 V / RCS. An RC filter (RCSF, CCSF) may be needed to suppress the leading-edge spike from rectifier recovery and parasitic capacitance; its time constant can be much shorter than the switching period, and must stay well below the minimum on-time.

Put a small resistor in series with CCT to ground and apply the sync pulse across it; the pulse lifts CCT past the upper threshold. Run the free oscillator about 20 % slower than the sync stream with a 0.5 V pulse. The local ramp stays available for slope compensation.

Either raise ISENSE above 1 V or pull COMP below two diode drops above ground; either makes the PWM comparator output high. Because the latch is reset-dominant, OUTPUT stays low until the clock after the shutdown condition is removed. An SCR can make the shutdown latch; it resets when VCC falls below the lower UVLO threshold and the reference turns off.

Converters running above 50 % duty need slope compensation. A part of the oscillator ramp, buffered by a transistor, is summed resistively into ISENSE; CCSF with RCSF also filters the leading-edge spike.

There is no internal soft start. An RC network charged from VREF and a PNP on COMP hold the error amplifier output low at power-up and release it as the capacitor charges, so the pulse width grows from zero; the transistor isolates the network from normal operation.

The CCT sawtooth fed into ISENSE instead of the switch current makes the PWM compare the error voltage with a fixed ramp. Loop compensation is like that of a voltage-mode controller, with differences from the low-output-resistance amplifier.

In normal operation the IC regulates peak current and duty cycle (current mode) or duty cycle only (voltage mode). In UVLO mode, before VCC reaches the turn-on threshold, VREF is not generated; a restart needs VCC above the turn-on threshold again.

The 48 W, 12 V flyback (Figure 8-2) uses the UC2842 because its duty cycle (0.627) exceeds 50 % and it is off-line. Chosen values: fSW 110 kHz with RRT 15.4 kΩ and CCT 1000 pF (a C0G/NP0 part for flat temperature coefficient); RSTART 100 kΩ (two 50 kΩ in series), giving 1 mA at low line; CVCC 120 µF for about 2 s start-up; CVREF 1 µF 16 V ceramic placed at VREF and GROUND; RG 10 Ω, a trade between EMI and switching loss; CCSF 100 pF; RCS 0.75 Ω for a 1.36 A peak. TL431 bias: 10 mA from the 10 V zener through RTLbias 1 kΩ; ROPTO 1 kΩ moves the opto pole out of the range of interest. The loop crosses over near 1.8 kHz with about 67° phase margin; check stability over all corners and tolerances.

Bypass VCC and VREF to ground with 0.1 µF to 1 µF ceramic capacitors at the pins. Off-line designs may need a larger VCC capacitor to hold VCC above the UVLO off threshold during start-up. A gate-to-source bleeder on the MOSFET is required.

Run the feedback trace direct and fairly wide, away from the inductor and noisy power traces, ideally on the far side of a ground plane from the inductor. Put the low-value VCC ceramic right at the pin; surface-mount parts lessen lead inductance. Keep the compensation parts close to the IC and away from switching traces, and VFB short with little stray capacitance. Make power traces short, direct and wide, at least 15 mils (0.381 mm) per ampere; keep the inductor, output capacitors and output diode close together. Tie the grounds of the IC, input and output capacitors and output diode to a ground plane; on multilayer boards a plane can separate the power layer from the signal layer, with about one standard via per 200 mA. Arrange the parts so that the switching current loops in both states circulate the same way. Return the timing capacitor to GROUND by a short, separate trace.
